name: Cyproheptadine + Tricholine Citrate
meta: Syrup and tablet (strengths not stated in product list)
Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride: First-generation antihistamine with antiserotonergic activity; Tricholine Citrate: Lipotropic / choleretic agent
Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride: R06AX02; Tricholine Citrate: Not assigned
Hydrochloride: Schedule H – prescription only; Tricholine Citrate: Ingredient of prescription combination
sections: White to slightly yellowish crystalline powder (hydrochloride), slightly soluble in water.
Quaternary ammonium (choline) salt of citric acid
White crystalline powder, freely soluble in water.

Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride: Also used off-label for serotonin syndrome and as an appetite stimulant; peak effect 1–4 hours. First approval/introduction: Patented 1959; introduced 1961 (Merck Sharp & Dohme). Tricholine Citrate: A water-soluble choline salt used to support hepatic fat mobilisation and bile secretion. First approval/introduction: Used as a lipotropic/choleretic agent in Indian combination products.
Syrup and tablet (strengths not stated in product list)
Cyproheptadine stimulates appetite via hypothalamic 5-HT2 antagonism; tricholine citrate aids fat digestion and liver function.

Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride Antagonises H1 histamine and 5-HT2 serotonin receptors; hypothalamic antiserotonergic action stimulates appetite. Receptor / target profile: First-generation H1 antagonist and potent 5-HT2A/2B antagonist (Ki 0.46–3.0 nM / 1.5–2.6 nM); anticholinergic and antidopaminergic activity.

Tricholine Citrate Choline source that promotes hepatic fat mobilisation (lipotropic) and increases bile secretion, aiding fat digestion; used with cyproheptadine as an appetite and digestion aid. Receptor / target profile: Lipotropic (choline donor) and choleretic actions.
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 6–9 h; extensively metabolised (glucuronide). Half-life ~8 h.
Choline incorporated into phosphatidylcholine; citrate enters Krebs cycle
Summary: Absorbed and utilised in phospholipid metabolism.
Loss of appetite and poor weight gain (after exclusion of underlying disease)
Adults: 10 mL syrup or 1 tablet three times daily before meals
Children 2–6 years: 2.5–5 mL two to three times daily; 6–14 years: 5 mL three times daily (cyproheptadine max 12 mg/day 2–6 yrs; 16 mg/day 7–14 yrs)
Review after 4–6 weeks; avoid prolonged use
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Contraindicated <2 years; 2–6 years max 12 mg/day; 7–14 years max 16 mg/day.
Use with caution in biliary obstruction.
Neonates, premature infants; children under 2 years
Children – may cause excitation, hallucinations or convulsions in overdose
Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride: Before meals; avoid alcohol.
Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride: CNS depression or stimulation (children: hallucinations, convulsions), anticholinergic effects. Supportive care. Tricholine Citrate: GI upset.
Studies of cyproheptadine show modest weight gain in underweight children and adults; evidence for the combination is limited.
Not for long-term use without review
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
